title: Guidelines for reinforcement learning in healthcare

content.abstract_summary: Establishes clinical and methodological guidelines for applying reinforcement learning in healthcare. Highlights the critical need for offline/batch RL, rigorous off-policy evaluation, handling of unobserved confounding (POMDPs), and safety bounds before clinical translation.
key_findings: Active exploration on real patients is unethical; clinical RL must be learned offline from observational data or validated mechanistic simulators
Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE) is mandatory to estimate policy performance reliably prior to clinical deployment
Identifies key pitfalls: partial observability, action space mismatch, unmeasured confounding, and unstable reward functions
Proposes reporting standards for clinical RL studies to ensure reproducibility and safety
limitations: Broad high-level guidelines; does not provide pharmacometric ODE-specific reward formulations

extracted_claims.text: Unlike games or robotics where agents learn through online exploration, reinforcement learning in healthcare must almost exclusively rely on observational data and offline evaluation.

gaps_addressed: Provides foundational clinical translation guidelines and OPE rationale for precision dosing in Pillar 3 (M3.4/M3.6)

provenance.notes: Added 2026-08-29 by Antigravity review. Foundational guideline for clinical RL and off-policy evaluation in Pillar 3.
